LEARN VOID / CONCURRENCY

Parallel workers

Move independent work onto bounded native workers.

Async execution

This example uses the explicit async host adapter. Its source is checked by the compiler; it is not a synchronous CLI entry program.

Choose parallel work explicitly

spawn calls a directly named synchronous noncapturing function on a native worker. Await its result from an async function. Arguments are evaluated before submission, and supported value data is transferred to the worker.

Keep the shared-state boundary small

The initial worker subset accepts scalars, strings and recursively safe fixed value data. Arbitrary mutable managed objects, task handles, callable values and native resources cannot be transferred between tasks this way. A worker can create its own private managed state.

Follow the data, not timing

The original packet keeps the caller’s later edit while the worker receives an independent value snapshot. The example also uses nested task groups and two small worker calculations. Input 5 returns 124 through the explicit async host adapter; it does not depend on which worker finishes first.
